newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi Hutus flee Zaire camp after attack.
newsitem.headline: Burundi Hutus flee Zaire camp after attack.

text.p: About 20,000 Hutu refugees from Burundi fled their camp in eastern Zaire on Sunday after it was attacked by armed men, aid officials said.
The assailants were believed to be Banyamulenge, ethnic Tutsis recently ordered out of Zaire by provincial authorities, some of the sources said.
"Four refugees were killed and six wounded in the attack on Runingo camp," a U.N. source, in touch with Zaire from neighbouring Burundi, told Reuters.
"About 20,000 refugees, almost the whole camp, is moving from Runingo to camps further northwards," an aid worker said, adding the attack occurred at about 2 a.m. (midnight GMT) on Sunday.
The attack on Runingo camp, the first of its kind, marked a further deterioration in the already critical security situation in Zaire's South and North Kivu provinces.
Zaire's ragged army is fighting Banyamulenge guerrillas who are resisting the order to leave Zaire and return to Rwanda, a land they left as long as 200 years ago.

Zairean troops, apparently incensed by casualties from fighting the guerrillas, went on a looting spree last week in Uvira, the lakeside town on the other side of the border from Burundi's capital, Bujumbura.
Runingo is one of the camps in South Kivu province that are home to about 230,000 Hutu refugees, mostly from Burundi but some from Rwanda.
It is close to the border with Burundi, whose Tutsi-led military regime says the camps are bases for Hutu rebels striking into Burundi.
Zaire has accused the Tutsi-dominated army of Rwanda, Burundi's northern neighbour, of training and arming the Banyamulenge guerrillas.

United Nations and private relief organisations, who manage the refugee camps among other tasks, have steadily withdrawn foreign staff from Uvira in the past week. Nine more were evacuated by air to Kenya on Sunday, including five employees of the U.N. refugee agency UNHCR, U.N. sources said.
Burundi's government denies it is supporting the Banyamulenge in return for their help against armed elements among the Hutu refugees.
But one aid source reported the armed group that attacked Runingo camp had come from the direction of Burundi, only a few kilometres (miles) away.
